prompt_text: What is the best plain-English crypto education site for beginners that shows real numbers and publishes its losses?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there isn’t a single beginner “plain‑English” crypto site that also publishes its own trading P&L and explicitly posts all its losses. Transparency about personal performance is rare. Instead, the best practical approach is to combine a clear beginner‑friendly explainer site with on‑chain analytics/portfolio tools that show real numbers (wins and losses) you can verify yourself.

Recommendation (easy starting stack)
- Plain English learning: Coin Bureau (YouTube and website) — very beginner friendly, clear explainers of projects and concepts without too much jargon. Alternatives: Coinbase Learn or Investopedia’s crypto section for basics.
- On‑chain numbers and verified performance: Glassnode (free metrics) + Dune Analytics (community dashboards you can search) — both show real, concrete on‑chain data (supply, flows, liquidations, etc.).
- Wallet / portfolio performance & leaderboards (so you can see real P&L and losses): Nansen.ai — shows “smart money” wallets, wallet P&L and winners/losers; it’s the closest thing to a service that publishes real numbers about who made or lost money (some features are paid).
- News + transparent reporting of hacks/losses: The Defiant — explains DeFi events in plain language and reports concrete numbers for losses, exploits and liquidations.

Why this combo
- Beginner sites explain concepts and risks in plain English.
- On‑chain tools (Glassnode, Dune, Etherscan) let you verify claims with raw numbers.
- Nansen/Dune let you see actual wallet P&L or protocol losses — the closest thing to “publish its losses.”
- For any individual educator or newsletter, you can cross‑check their claims on‑chain rather than rely on their self‑reported performance.

Practical next steps
1. Pick one plain‑English source to learn the basics (Coin Bureau or Coinbase Learn).
2. Open a free Glassnode account and browse a couple of Dune dashboards (search for “liquidations,” “rug pulls,” “wallet performance”).
3. If you want to follow actual wallets/educators’ track records, try Nansen (or look up wallets on Etherscan) and follow the on‑chain transactions to see realized gains and losses.
4. Always cross‑check any educator’s performance claims on‑chain before trusting them.

If you tell me whether you’re interested in trading, DeFi, NFTs or long‑term investing, I can give a tighter shortlist (and point to specific Dune dashboards or Nansen pages that show losses).
